title: PHLPP1 inhibition in vascular smooth muscle cells alleviates atherosclerotic plaque formation via up-regulating autophagy in ApoE−/− mice
desc: PH domain and leucine-rich repeat protein phosphatase1 (PHLPP1) is a recently identified serine/threonine protein phosphatase which plays a critical role in metabolic disorders through dephosphorylation of its downstream targets, but the association between PHLPP1 and atherosclerosis as well as vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC)-derived foam cell formation remains poorly understood. This study investigates the function and mechanisms of PHLPP1 inhibition in atherosclerotic plaque progression and VSMC-derived foam cell formation. In vivo, the expression of PHLPP1 in ApoE−/− mice was knocked down by lentivirus-mediated short hairpin RNA (shRNA). HE staining, Oil Red O staining, immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence of aortic sinus sections were performed. Similarly, in vitro, the expression of PHLPP1 was inhibited using PHLPP1-siRNA; and then the primary VSMCs were exposed to 80 µg/ml oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL) for the following experiments. The expression of PHLPP1 was up-regulated in both atherosclerotic plaques and ox-LDL treated primary VSMCs. Furthermore, PHLPP1 inhibition ameliorated the atherosclerotic plaque formation in high-fat diet fed ApoE−/− mice (atherosclerosis model) independent of LDL-C levels. Additionally, PHLPP1 knockdown reduced the lipid accumulation and improved the autophagy level in VSMCs mediated by activating AMPK signaling pathway, which could be blocked by 3-MA (an autophagy inhibitor) and compound C (an AMPK inhibitor). Inhibition of PHLPP1 expression alleviates atherosclerotic plaque progression and ameliorates lipid deposition in VSMCs, an effect associated with enhanced autophagy mediated by increased AMPK phosphorylation in advanced atherosclerosis.

title: RFAs: Integrated Nutrition Programme for Karamoja Communities (Uganda)
desc: Deadline: 20-Aug-2026 The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) Uganda is inviting applications from organisations to support community-based nutrition, food security, livelihoods, and resilience activities in Karamoja. The programme aims to improve access to safe, diverse, nutritious, and affordable food while strengthening malnutrition prevention and treatment, WASH practices, social protection, livelihoods, and community-led nutrition services.
